title: The Lobby Where Arrival Ends

features.name: registration-desk
features.desc-on-touch: The desk where you give your name and forget why you came. The clerk is helpful but unable to say what hotel this is. No one can remember the address.

features.name: key-hooks
features.desc-on-touch: Numbered pegs holding keys to rooms in this building—or another. The numbers go high but the floors stop at two.

features.name: waiting-seating
features.desc-on-touch: Plastic chairs arranged in a configuration that suggests you have already been waiting. Your suitcase is beside you. You do not remember setting it down.

features.name: elevator-shaft
features.desc-on-touch: A shaft descends. The elevator does not come. The button light has been on since before you arrived.

features.name: clock-face
features.desc-on-touch: The time it shows is always the time you arrived, but you cannot remember what time that was.

inscription: the hallway learned to return to itself, and then taught you that staying is just another word for patience

reverie.title: REVERIE — the lobby where nothing arrives
narr: You sit with Leif in these plastic chairs, both of you waiting
for something that was supposed to happen at three o'clock.
It is three o'clock. It has always been three o'clock.
Leif says: the building is still learning what it is.
You say: we are still learning what we came for.
The elevator button glows. It will glow until you both leave.

file.name: Arrival_Record_Unnamed_Establishment_Undated.txt
file.note: A guest register entry with no date, no signature, no room number. Just: 'Came here. Waiting. Building has not yet decided what to be.' The handwriting is not in Leif's hand or Katita's.

exits.label: back up the corridor that learned to return to itself
down to the basement where arrivals are filed
through the side entrance to the courtyard that forgets its geometry
